Who we are 

About Stripe / Metronome 

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Metronome is the leading usage-based billing platform built for modern software companies. With Metronome, now a Stripe product, companies can launch products faster, offer any pricing model, and streamline finance workflows without writing code.

Our platform computes hundreds of millions of invoices per billing period and continues to scale rapidly to accommodate new customers. We save them days of development time and manual invoicing, enabling them to use their billing data to better serve their customers. Our customers love our product and approach, and we’re humbled to work with amazing companies like OpenAI, Hubspot, NVIDIA, Confluent, Anthropic, and many others.

You'll be joining an experienced team that includes founders who have successfully built and sold startups, alongside Stripes with direct experience scaling teams through hypergrowth at companies like Dropbox, Palantir, and MongoDB. You'll be joining Stripe and be part of the holistic Stripe platform approaching monetization.

About the team

The Solutions Engineering team at Metronome is a technical group that sits at the intersection of everything Metronome does: sales, account management, product, R&D, and operations. Bottom line, we own the technical side of the customer lifecycle from the very first discovery call through demos, POC, technical scoping, and handover to our post-sales groups. We act like a producer to get the show running with Metronome. This role will train you to grow across these vectors.

What you’ll do

As a member of the Solutions Engineering team, your first month will be:

  • Learning to tell a clear value story about how and where Metronome solves challenges and creates opportunities in a modern monetization stack.
  • Assisting in planning, building, and running customized demos of Metronome for buyers with many different personas (engineering, product management, operations, finance, etc).

In your first 3 months, you can expect to:

  • Become proficient in what discovery is and using it to understand what challenges our prospects face
  • Travel to meet prospects in the field. Workshops, conferences, on-sites — we believe in meeting our customers in-person whenever possible. Anywhere in the world.
  • Land deals for some of the most exciting names in software, from startups to enterprise SaaS.

In 6 months you’ll be:

  • Owning knowledge areas, projects, tools, and market segments in the Solutions Engineering team.
  • Running tight Proofs of Concept with clearly-defined success criteria that get us to the technical win.
  • Representing the Solutions Engineering group as a deal team member on your own.
  • Handling detailed scoping to ensure that customers are set up for success post-sales.

In your first year you’ll have:

  • Built relationships with people at our prospect organizations, from day-to-day operators to C-Suite executives.
  • Designed integrations of Metronome into prospect systems and acted as a pricing and packaging consultant, influencing the direction of our future customers.

As a fast-moving unit within Stripe, there’s a lot still to figure out and tremendous room for high-agency people to have impact and make a difference. If this excites you as much as it excites us, let’s talk.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 1-3 years of experience working in technical and/or customer-facing roles involving SaaS products (for example, roles like engineering, solutions, technical account management/consulting). Academic background in a technical area with high EQ is also sought after.
  • Relentless passion for being a hand-raiser. Big challenges are exciting, small tasks are an opportunity for a win. From landing big clients to simply cleaning up an old dashboard you’re interested in learning and getting things done.
  • Growth mindset is critical in being able to learn new things quickly, adapt on the fly, and operate in fast-moving startup environments that value high agency.
  • Exceptional communication skills -- technical, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders should all feel like comfortable counterparts in conversing with you.
  • Excitement for building and improving GTM playbooks and processes. 

Preferred qualifications  

  • Knowledge of the quote-to-cash space, including integrating with or otherwise interacting with tools like Salesforce, NetSuite, CPQs, etc.
  • Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in other technical roles.
  • Experience in a pure sales role, particularly selling to technical buyers in engineering and product organizations or selling as a founding or early salesperson at a startup.
  • Experience with logs, metrics, billing, finance, or other infrastructure or financial tooling and concepts.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.
 

About the Team

OKX’s Global Legal team provides strategic legal, regulatory, and policy guidance to OKX and its affiliated entities across jurisdictions and business lines. The team partners closely with stakeholders across Compliance, Product, Communications, Operations, and the broader business to support responsible growth in a rapidly evolving global regulatory environment.
 
We are a collaborative, high-performing, and fast-paced team that values practical judgment, intellectual curiosity, and clear communication. Our global team of more than 60 lawyers works across multiple regions, with the Chief Legal Officer based in the United States.
 

About the Role

We are seeking a Government Relations & Public Policy Manager to support OKX’s engagement with U.S. policymakers, regulators, industry stakeholders, and external advocacy partners. This is a high-visibility, execution-oriented role at the intersection of policy, regulation, licensing, and business strategy.
 
Reporting to a senior member of the Legal Department and working closely with external advisors including lobbying, policy, and legal partners, you will help advance OKX’s U.S. policy and regulatory priorities across federal and, where relevant, state-level issues affecting crypto and digital assets. You will translate regulatory developments into practical insights, coordinate external engagement, and work cross-functionally to ensure policy considerations are reflected in business decisions.
 
This role is well suited to a thoughtful, highly organized policy professional who is ready to build depth in digital-assets regulation and take increasing ownership of key workstreams.
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Support the development and execution of OKX’s U.S. government relations and public-policy strategy.
  • Monitor and analyze federal and state legislative, regulatory, and political developments relevant to crypto, financial services, market structure, consumer protection, AML, sanctions, and technology.
  • Distill complex policy and regulatory developments into clear, actionable briefings for Legal, Compliance, Product, Communications, and business teams.
  • Assist in creating materials for licensing, regulatory, and government meetings, including briefing books, presentations, talking points, background research, stakeholder profiles, and follow-up summaries.
  • Help prepare regulatory submissions, consultation responses, policy memos, comment letters, and other external-facing materials.
  • Partner closely with external lobbying firms to coordinate advocacy priorities, meeting preparation, intelligence gathering, and follow-up across federal and state policy workstreams.
  • Help plan and execute Hill Days, including stakeholder outreach, meeting scheduling, briefing materials, participant preparation, and post-meeting tracking.
  • Manage day-to-day engagement with relevant trade associations, coalitions, and industry working groups; identify opportunities to advance OKX’s policy priorities.
  • Represent or support OKX at policy conferences, regulatory roundtables, industry events, and other external forums.
  • Support the company’s PAC advisory activities, including policy research, stakeholder mapping, meeting preparation, and administration in partnership with the Global CLO, Legal team, and external advisors.
  • Build and maintain productive working relationships with policymakers, regulators, congressional staff, industry groups, and other external stakeholders.
  • Support meetings involving senior company leaders and external stakeholders, including preparation, attendance where appropriate, follow-up, and tracking of commitments.
  • Maintain organized records of external engagements, policy developments, advocacy priorities, and key commitments.
 

What We Look For In You

  • 6+ years of relevant experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, law, financial services, or a related field.
  • Familiarity with U.S. financial-services regulation and the policy issues shaping crypto and digital assets.
  • Experience working with government, a regulator, Congress, a trade association, policy consultancy, law firm, lobbying firm, or a regulated financial-services or technology company.
  • Strong research, analytical, writing, and presentation skills; able to make complex issues accessible to non-specialist audiences.
  • Experience producing polished meeting materials, stakeholder briefings, policy memos, and presentations under tight deadlines.
  • Excellent project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain close attention to detail.
  • Sound judgment, discretion, and a collaborative approach to working across functions.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where policy and business priorities can evolve quickly.
  • A genuine interest in the future of digital assets, financial innovation, and responsible regulation.
 

Nice to Haves

  • Existing working relationships with relevant U.S. policy, regulatory, or industry stakeholders.
  • Experience drafting comment letters, consultation responses, or other policy advocacy materials.
  • Experience coordinating Hill Days, policy events, trade-association participation, or external lobbying partners.
  • Knowledge of crypto market structure, stablecoins, payments, custody, or AML/sanctions policy.

  • Work closely with the Global CLO, senior leaders, external advisors, and experienced policy, legal, compliance, and business partners.

About Matter Labs

Matter Labs invented ZK rollups and built the first one on Ethereum: six years in production, over a billion transactions processed, over four billion dollars in value locked. We want programmable money to become a foundation for the next financial system, with institutions able to shape the services they provide and keep authority as their infrastructure evolves.

Prividium is our platform for institutions to build and operate digital asset businesses, with privacy and under their own rules. Prividium Commander is the control plane for digital asset services: an institution decides who can do what and tracks the resulting activity, on Prividium Ledger or on the chains it already runs. Prividium Ledger is a private blockchain with publicly verifiable execution. Prividium Connect gives institutions private, bridgeless transactions across blockchains.

Prividium Ledger runs in production for a number of institutional customers. Keeping those ledgers reliable, and making the next ten cheaper to operate than the first four, is the work this role is hired for.

Remote and global, few approvals, a CEO you can reach, unrestricted access to the best AI tools and the expectation that you use them, and a hiring bar of hell yes or no.

The role

You join the Production Unit, the three-person team that owns ZKsync OS in production for our customers: detection, incidents, rollouts and the service objectives each customer is measured against. Today the work is mostly reactive: on-call, incidents, rollouts, RCAs. The job is to change that. Every page and every manual step is a candidate for a fix in the server, a better alert or an automation. About 30 percent of your time goes to code now, and that share grows as the reactive load shrinks.

You own the environments you are assigned end to end: whether a change is safe to roll out, how an incident gets restored and explained, and whether the customer's service objectives are being met. Component teams own their code; you read it, find the cause, and land the fix.

What you will do:

  • Run production for institutional customers. Hold the First Responder rotation, coordinate incidents to restoration, and write the RCA the customer's engineers read.

  • Decide what ships. Go/no-go on changes to your environments, verification before rollout and validation after, including executing sequencer rollouts.

  • Remove the cause. Turn pages, runbooks and manual steps into fixes in the sequencer, provers or tooling, so the same incident does not come back.

  • Measure the service. Own the SLA card for your customers, measured monthly against their contracts.

  • Finish across teams. Drive diagnosis and fixes through the component teams that own the code, without waiting to be asked.

  • Later, support customers who run the chain themselves, where the fix has to work in someone else's hands.

Within a year, on-call load in your environments is measurably lower because of what you shipped, and the unit can take on the next customer without adding people.

What we look for

  • You have been on-call for a system you wrote code for, and you have owned an incident from page to RCA to the fix that stopped it recurring.

  • You find causes in code you did not write. Strong in a systems language such as Rust, Go, C++ or Java; Rust is learnable here.

  • You verify before you roll out and you can say which changes are reversible and which are not.

  • You have run production for a service with external customers, and your incident notices and RCAs were read by their engineers.

  • You make other teams finish the work without escalating.

  • You are willing to hold a 24/7 rotation.

Nice to have: rollup or node operations experience (sequencer, prover, L1 settlement); Ethereum execution client internals; tooling you built that other teams adopted.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.

Not this role

This is not a Forward Deployed Engineer role, which builds and deploys for a customer from discovery to production readiness; this role operates what is in production. It is not DevOps (clusters, network, L1 nodes, backups and disaster recovery stay with DevOps), not partner management, and not a people-management role.

Compensation and work model

  • Base salary range: USD 192,000 to 230,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. For candidates in the EU the same range applies

  • Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

  • Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

  • Fully remote. You must be based in the US or the EU, with the US preferred; some of our customers whitelist the jurisdictions their operators work from, so this is a hard requirement.

  • Full-time, as an employee or a contractor.

  • 24/7 First Responder rotation shared with the Production Unit. Everyone in this role is on it.

  • We do not ask about your current or past pay at any stage of the process.
